answer: Cross-epoch drift scoring: each identity's behavioural fingerprint (task mix, timing, counterparties) is hashed per epoch, and the score compares consecutive hashes, weighted so stable traits form a slow nebula of baseline features. A large discontinuity flags the identity and routes its rewards through a holding period until two epochs of consistent behaviour confirm it. The cost: an attacker rotating identities pays a tide of forfeited rewards each time a new fingerprint fails to match, since fresh identities carry no history.
